description: Validates PRD, requirements registry, OT linkage, and evidence traceability through business-health.

capabilities.label: PRD Contract
capabilities.description: PRD.md exists and conforms to the canonical template: required sections and priority tiers present, no unknown sections, section content substantive, operational-target lines well-formed.

levels.name: PRD unavailable
levels.description: PRD.md is missing or unreadable; the scenario states no product intent.
levels.capability_summary: Business Health cannot evaluate the scenario's stated intent.
levels.next_unlock: A PRD.md at the scenario root.

levels.name: PRD present
levels.description: PRD.md exists but required template sections or priority tiers are missing.
levels.capability_summary: Intent is stated but not in the canonical, machine-checkable shape.
levels.next_unlock: All required template sections and P0/P1/P2 operational-target tiers present.

levels.name: Template conformant
levels.description: All required sections exist; remaining findings are content-level (placeholders, thin sections, unknown headings, malformed OT IDs).
levels.capability_summary: The PRD is structurally sound and safe for tooling to parse.
levels.next_unlock: Section content substantive, no unknown sections, canonical OT ID format.

levels.name: PRD clean
levels.capability_summary: The PRD is a trustworthy statement of intent.

capabilities.label: Requirements Registry
capabilities.description: requirements/ exists and is structurally sound: parseable index + modules, unique IDs, acyclic imports, resolvable refs, valid statuses, no starter-template residue, every requirement carrying validation.

levels.name: Registry unavailable
levels.capability_summary: The scenario makes no machine-checkable requirement claims.
levels.next_unlock: A parseable requirements/index.json with at least one module.

levels.name: Registry parseable
levels.description: The registry parses but has structural integrity findings (duplicate IDs, cycles, orphaned refs, missing ids) or is still the starter template.
levels.capability_summary: Requirement claims exist but cannot all be trusted.
levels.next_unlock: No structural integrity findings; starter template replaced with scenario-specific requirements.

levels.name: Registry honest
levels.description: Structure is sound; remaining findings are quality-level (missing titles, invalid status vocabulary, requirements without validation, README drift).
levels.capability_summary: The registry is a structurally trustworthy claim set.
levels.next_unlock: Every requirement titled, valid statuses, at least one validation entry each.

levels.name: Registry clean
levels.capability_summary: The registry is a complete, falsifiable claim set.

capabilities.label: Intent Linkage
capabilities.description: The OT ↔ requirement ↔ validation spine holds in both directions: every prd_ref resolves to a real operational target, every P0/P1 target has requirements, every validation ref exists on disk.

levels.name: Linkage unevaluable
levels.description: PRD.md or the requirements registry is missing, so the linkage join cannot run.
levels.next_unlock: Both a PRD and a parseable registry.

levels.name: Spine joinable
levels.description: The join runs but linkage findings exist: dangling prd_refs, orphaned operational targets, or validation refs that resolve to nothing.
levels.capability_summary: Intent and implementation claims are partially connected.
levels.next_unlock: Every prd_ref resolves, every P0/P1 target is covered, every code-typed ref exists.

levels.name: Spine linked
levels.description: Both linkage directions are clean on current artifacts.
levels.capability_summary: Stated outcomes and requirement claims form a closed, navigable graph.

levels.name: Linkage clean
levels.capability_summary: The intent spine is fully closed.

capabilities.label: Evidence Traceability
capabilities.description: Requirement statuses are earned from evidence: sync snapshots fresh relative to the latest suite run, manual attestations unexpired, no checked-off outcome without passing linked evidence, no hand-edited statuses.

levels.name: No evidence
levels.description: No requirements-sync snapshot or manual-validation ledger exists for the scenario.
levels.next_unlock: A comprehensive suite run producing a sync snapshot, or logged manual attestations.

levels.name: Evidence present
levels.description: Evidence artifacts exist but honesty findings remain: unproven checked-off outcomes or statuses that contradict the sync writer.
levels.capability_summary: Some claims are evidence-backed; some are not honest.
levels.next_unlock: No unproven claims; every status earned, not asserted.

levels.name: Claims honest
levels.description: All statuses are earned; remaining findings are freshness-level (stale snapshot, expired manual attestations).
levels.capability_summary: The contract tells the truth as of its last evidence.

levels.name: Evidence fresh
levels.description: Evidence traceability checks are clean and current.

prd_missing_prd.reason: Authoring a PRD is a product decision; the wizard scaffolds one interactively but a human or calling agent supplies the intent.

prd_template_unexpected_sections.reason: An unknown heading may be misnamed canon or intentional scenario-specific content; deciding which requires judgment.

prd_template_content.reason: Filling placeholder or thin sections with truthful product content is judgment the calling agent owns.

business_starter_template.reason: Replacing starter requirements with real, falsifiable claims is product judgment; the wizard assists but does not decide.

business_duplicate_req_id.reason: Which duplicate keeps the ID is meaningful — evidence history and prd_refs hang off it.

business_import_cycle.reason: Breaking a dependency cycle requires deciding which relationship is wrong.

business_orphaned_ref.reason: A dangling child/depends_on ref means either the ref or the missing requirement is the bug; deciding which is judgment.

business_req_missing_id.reason: Requirement IDs are stable evidence anchors; minting one belongs to the author, not a fixer.

business_req_missing_title.reason: A title is a behavioral claim summary only the author can state truthfully.

business_req_no_validation.reason: Only a real test or attestation proves a claim; scaffolding a fake validation entry would be gaming the ladder.

intent.prd_ref_unmatched.reason: Whether the operational target or the requirement's prd_ref is wrong is a product decision; only trivial ID-format drift is mechanical and that is covered by prd_ot_id_format.

intent.ref_missing.reason: The correct target of a broken validation ref (renamed test, moved file, or dead claim) requires knowing which side moved.

business_unproven_claim.reason: An outcome checked off without passing linked evidence is either premature or missing tests; both need judgment, never an automatic uncheck.

business_status_unearned.reason: A status contradicting the sync writer means someone asserted progress; reverting must be a conscious correction, not a silent rewrite.

business_evidence_stale.reason: Freshening evidence means running the suite (test-genie owns that run); business-health only reports the staleness.

business_manual_expired.reason: Re-attesting a manual validation requires actually performing it; manual-log records the new attestation.

business_registry_unparseable.reason: Repairing broken JSON or a dangling import requires reading what the author meant; a fixer would guess.
